dripSeries.subject: Welcome to the family of God! (Your first steps)
dripSeries.preview: You took the most important step of your life today. Here is what just happened...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

First of all: welcome home. 

When you prayed and surrendered your heart to Jesus Christ, something cosmic took place. The Bible tells us that 'if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away; behold, the new has come' (2 Corinthians 5:17).

You might feel a surge of peace, or you might not feel emotionally different at all—and that is completely normal. Faith is anchored in the steadfast promise of God, not in fluctuating emotions. Your sins are forgiven, your debt is wiped clean, and you are officially adopted as a beloved child of God.

Today, do just one simple thing: thank Jesus for loving you enough to give His life for you.

We are walking right beside you.

With warm love,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: Talking with God: Prayer made simple
dripSeries.preview: You don't need poetic language or stained glass to talk with your Father...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

Many people think prayer requires elaborate vocabulary or religious formulas. But Jesus taught that prayer is simply an honest conversation with a Father who already loves you.

A helpful way to begin is the ACTS model:
• A - Adoration: Tell God what you admire about Him (His kindness, patience, majesty).
• C - Confession: Be honest about where you stumbled today. He doesn't condemn you; He cleanses you.
• T - Thanksgiving: Name 3 specific things you are grateful for.
• S - Supplication: Ask Him for what you need—peace, guidance, strength for your family.

Take 3 quiet minutes right now to speak with Him in your own words. He is listening.

With you on the journey,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: Opening the Word: Where to begin reading the Bible
dripSeries.preview: The Bible isn't a textbook; it is God's personal love letter to humanity...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

Opening a 66-book library like the Bible can feel intimidating at first. If you start on page 1 in Genesis, you might get bogged down in ancient genealogical records.

Our recommendation: start in the Gospel of John in the New Testament.

John was one of Jesus's closest earthly companions. He wrote with one single heartbeat: 'These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name' (John 20:31).

Try reading just one chapter a day. Before you read, whisper: 'Holy Spirit, speak to my heart through these words.'

Cheering you on,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: When doubts or old habits whisper in your ear
dripSeries.preview: Becoming a Christian doesn't make you instantly immune to temptation or questions...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

It is common in your first week to experience moments where old habits pull at you, or a nagging thought whispers: 'Did that decision really change anything?'

Please hear this loud and clear: temptation is not sin; yielding is. And when you do stumble, do not run away from God in shame—run straight into His embrace in repentance.

Romans 8:1 reminds us: 'There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.'

Your standing with God does not depend on your perfection; it rests on Christ's finished work on the Cross.

Standing with you in grace,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: Finding your spiritual family (Why church matters)
dripSeries.preview: God never designed anyone to live the Christian walk in isolation...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

Imagine taking a burning coal out of a glowing campfire and setting it alone on the cold dirt. Within minutes, the flame dies out. But keep that coal surrounded by other embers, and it stays hot and radiant for hours.

That is why the local church matters. The church is not a building or a performance; it is a family of imperfect people following a perfect Savior together.

Look for a local, Bible-believing church near you this week where the Gospel of grace is preached and people love one another genuinely. If you need help finding one in your area, simply reply to this email and our team will gladly assist you!

Warmly,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: Sharing your story with someone you love
dripSeries.preview: The most powerful sermon you will ever preach is your own transformed life...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

You don't need a theology degree to tell someone about Jesus. In John chapter 9, a man born blind was healed by Jesus. When religious leaders interrogated him, he gave the most honest testimony in history: 'One thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!'

Think about one person in your circle—a family member, colleague, or friend carrying heavy burdens. You don't have to preach at them; just share what Jesus has done in your heart with gentleness and respect.

Your story carries hope for someone walking in darkness.

With great joy,
Your Outreach Care Team

dripSeries.subject: Walking in grace every single day
dripSeries.preview: This isn't the finish line; it is the beginning of an eternal adventure...
dripSeries.body:
Dear friend,

You have completed your first week of walking with Christ! 

Remember: spiritual growth is like a tree growing deep roots. It doesn't happen in a noisy rush, but through quiet, daily surrender. As Colossians 2:6-7 says: 'Just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him, strengthened in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.'

Our outreach team remains here for you. Whenever you need prayer, encouragement, or questions answered, visit our community prayer wall or connect with our pastoral counselors.

You are deeply loved, forever secure, and never alone.

In Christ's boundless love,
Your Outreach Care Team
